title: Given just one frame, can MiniMax H3 rebuild a 15-second dance video with sound?
summary: Yes. Hand frame 1 of the original clip to MiniMax H3 in local ComfyUI and it produces a 15.08-second dance video, with the background music generated by the model along with the picture (the qwen original's BGM was synthesized by a program after the fact). The model can only output 5–15 seconds per run, so the 30-second original came back as 15 seconds this time.
tags: Audio generated along with the picture
stats: Rebuilt the qwen-original dance video with MiniMax H3 in local ComfyUI (the fp8 build: weights squashed to 8-bit precision), then compared the two finished videos side by side. The attached speed-up model is the 8-step Turbo LoRA (a small model that pushes generation down to 8 steps).
Where the first frame came from

Took frame 1 straight from the original cut and scaled it to 704×960 (picture width×height in pixels) as the input image. Image-to-video means giving the model one picture and letting it turn that picture into a video; using the original frame keeps the character lined up with the original.

H3 produces the audio in the same generation run as the picture, with the prompt calling for a J-pop dance track. The qwen original's background music was synthesized by a program after the video was done, so the two sounds come from different sources.

H3 was only ever trained on 124–362 frames, which at 24fps (24 frames per second) works out to 5–15 seconds. One run can't fit the 30-second original, so this output is 15 seconds: 30s ▮▮▮▮▮ → 15s ▮▮▮
Where the stuff lives, and can you reproduce it

The finished video (15.08s · 704×960 @24fps · H.264+AAC · 3.4 MB), the workflow JSON and the input first frame are archived together in experiments/miku-h3-i2v/ — follow the files and it reproduces in one click.
findings: The whole pipeline runs in four steps: load the H3 model (UNETLoader) → attach the 8-step Turbo LoRA for speed → the image-to-video node MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo makes the picture → assemble the video file at 24fps (CreateVideo).
Pitfall 1: don't just grab any text encoder to read the prompt. qwen_3_8b doesn't match this model (512 vs 5120); you must switch to its matching dedicated encoder, qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3.
Pitfall 2: the speed-up models come in resolution tiers, and the wrong tier means a wasted run. The turbo 4-step LoRA only fits 768p; for high resolutions like this one you must use 8-step v1.0.
Pitfall 3: uploading an image to ComfyUI must use multipart/form-data (the chunked upload format web forms use); on PowerShell 5.1 it only goes through with curl.exe -F.
